comment: Extremely difficult to understand, spends the whole class deriving equations rather than teaching us actually how to use them. Gives us lots of very hard homework that is nowhere near good practice for the tests and quizzes. Not very accessible outside of class. Does not explain things clearly- not sure I learned anything this semester tbh.

Very unclear and unattainable expectations. Extremely lecture heavy and will lecture on new material up to less than 48 hours before exam is given with new material expected to be mastered for the exam. No practice materials given and no flexibility on assignments, exam dates, or curves. Attitude while answering questions isn't encouraging.

She is not an effective communicator, often going in long winded tangents and talks at you instead of to you. She also seems to get frustrated easily, which does not encourage question asking and does not create a conducive learning environment. She's smart no doubt but not a good educator.

She was very accessible outside of the class. Physics is not easy for me, but somehow she built up my confidence during the semester and I was able to learn the hard content. There is a lot to learn in this class and I would recommend this professor.

Dr. Dias is really invested in her students and always willing to go the extra mile to help you understand the material. That said, most of the lectures were focused on derivations rather than how to solve homework/test problems, so you have to devote a lot of time outside the class to learning the material.

Dr. Dias is a really nice and patient professor! She is always willing to help me outside the class. She really cares about students and their feedback to improve her teaching. The materials is not easy but doing practice exams is really helpful. Going to her office hour is really helpful too! I would recommend taking physics with her!

Dr. Dias is an amazing professor! She is very passionate about what she teaches, and it is clear that she wants all of her students to succeed. She is very receptive to student feedback and always willing to meet with you if you need help. The class was challenging at times, but I learned a lot and would highly recommend taking physics with her!

Dr. Dias is very math heavy. Be prepared to need to go to office hours a lot to understand the math. That said she is not much harder than the other professors, she just has hard tests. She is more than willing to spend as much time as you need to understand the content and is very good at one on one tutoring.

Dr Dias was really good at explaining all of the math that you have to learn in this class. It wasn't the easiest class I've taken (there's a ton of material to cover), but she gave me such a good background for my other physics classes. She is super nice and her office hours were very helpful. Class moves quick, but the exams were fine!

I really enjoyed Dr. Dias for classical mechanics! There was a semester long group project, which made it a lot more hands on than some of the other upper levels. Lectures were interesting. There were weekly quizzes based on the homework & exams were very reasonable. Not too difficult for an upper level physics course, and I learned a lot!
Dr. Diaz was a fair grader. She was understanding, kind, and always willing to go the extra mile for her students. I thoroughly enjoyed being her student.

Dr. Dias is super passionate about the subject & her lectures were always very interesting! Exams were very reasonable difficulty & fairly graded. She was very approachable and accessible outside of class. Would recommend!

Dr. Diaz is a really awesome person, but I would not recommend taking her. Exams are harshly graded (semi-fair), but the daily homework is always assigned on topics before they are actually taught. The labs were insane, not in their difficulty, but in how many (>30) and how tedious they were (might be a physics thing). She is very nice tho ( -_-')

Her lectures are obscure and all big picture oriented. You have to teach yourself everything outside of class. She was not available anytime outside of her office hours. Her tests were very hard. Good luck...
If you've never taken physics before, good luck. If you have some physics background, try to remember as much as you can. And good luck.

She is awful. Doesn't know how to explain physics and speeds through the material. She gives quizzes literally 5 minutes after you learn new material in class. Avoid her if your can. Not worth the suffering. She honestly should not be a professor.

She moves too fast and seems frustrated when students don't understand. The homework is always far more advanced than the lectures and the way she grades tests doesn't make any sense. While she's pretty good during office hours, the class itself is awful and makes many students taking it feel hopeless about physics.
The class was tough but she is very well prepared and made it very accessible. I will take any class with her again.
She is very good

Do yourself a favor and do not take this class with Dr. Dias. She makes it much harder than it needs to be, lectures are confusing and she is a very harsh grader. Quizzes and tests are often on content not covered in class. Class does not make sense and you will have to learn on your own

I know she is new and all, but she is very confusing, and at times, seems to baby us. She spends too much time on the basic concepts, and her test and quizzes do not match what you learned in class. She is probably one of the nicest professors in the department, and she's not boring in any sense, but she is just not quite yet there.

She is awesome. She makes sure you understand every step of the way and is great at keeping you engaged. She has a really fun personality and loves to laugh. Homework isn't that much and weekly quizzes are taken with notes allowed. Would Recommend

She was phenomenal but also new; still learning what she could do and expect. She is rapidly improving and eager to get better as a professor and work with you to make sure you can succeed. Good balance between mathematical explanations and the actual physics.

She has a great personality, and is actually excited to teach and loves Physics clearly, but she is just not that great at just teaching. She has a lot of expectations, so she really wants you to learn fast. Her accent might confuse you once in a while but not a problem.
